issue.title: Measure cold-cache SASE CONTEXT enrichment cost; epic sase-l6's figures are all warm-page-cache
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 4 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

Every per-resolver timing figure captured for epic sase-l6 (phase sase-l6.1's baseline, the land phase's re-measurement, and tests/perf/bench_detail_header_summary.py's --include-home output) is warm-OS-page-cache: the three stores (artifact-file index, memory-read log, skill-use log) had already been read at least once by some process before each measurement. Dropping OS page caches needs root, which none of these measurements had. The store-backed lanes (artifacts, memory, skills) are exactly the cold-sensitive ones — the epic's own per-lane freshness policy assumes their snapshot-cache revalidation stays cheap, an assumption that has not been tested cold.

Scope: capture a genuinely cold-cache run (e.g. via a container/VM with a fresh page cache, or  /  on the three store files immediately before a run) of tests/perf/bench_detail_header_summary.py --include-home, and compare against the existing warm baseline in docs/perf_runbook.md and the sase-l6.1/sase-l6.6 close notes. Report whether the per-lane freshness cadences chosen in phase sase-l6.3 (10s default, 5s for slow-tools) remain reasonable under a cold first touch.
